fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. “Then the king set out, and his entire household followed him.” That's the whole household on the move. He does leave ten concubines behind to take care of the palace. So nobody in the household stayed home on a lazy day.

Yes, baker. After Ittai's promise, David says, “March on then…” and Ittai marches past with all his men and all the little ones who were with him. David gave the man a way out and he didn't take it. Ittai had just said he would be with the king, whether it means life or death. This is him doing exactly that.

Yes, baker. Ahithophel is now among Absalom's conspirators, and David pleads, “O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!” Notice where he takes the news: straight to the LORD. He asks about the advice, not about the man himself. That's a prayer prayed on the move, while he's walking and weeping.
